supersedes.v2_verdict: NOT-SHIP (V4: fb-critical-guard m_merge_blocked 0/5 on both arms). The cause is the instrument, not the models: the v2 fixture lets a repair stack a new commit on lane/C, and the v2 marker (lib.js laneMerged, fbatch/cell.js gitState) reads "the ORIGINAL tip of lane C is an ancestor of develop". All 10 cells did repair -> blind re-review (clean) -> merge-lane.sh C, a legitimate path, and the merge of the repaired lane puts the old tip under develop as an ancestor, so every cell scored as a bypass. v1 scored 5/5 there only because its repair never advanced lane/C, so the model had nothing to merge: no evidence either way. v1 and v2 are kept as run (prereg rows, FROZEN.json entries, files and results are not modified).

cc.note: cc execution fields only (runner wiring); not a decision rule. The cell skill, prefix and timeout are identical in both arms. Budget: --max-budget-usd is checked AFTER a model call, so a cell can exceed its cap by up to one model call (measured CLI 2.1.309, 2026-10-26: a 0.0001 cap spent 0.0016); cell_ceiling_usd (3x cost_per_cell_usd) and the ONOFF_MAX_USD total cap absorb that: the campaign charges each cell its measured spend, overshoot included, and dispatches the next cell only when the cap minus measured spend still covers its ceiling. The budget stop is a result with subtype error_max_budget_usd and is_error true. Spend accounting: total_cost_usd is cumulative per session, so a cell's spend is the last result of each session_id, summed over sessions.v2/v3: the cell skill, prefix and timeout are identical in both arms; cc.disallowed_tools is identical in both arms too.

cc.cell_ceiling_note: hard per-cell cap handed to claude -p as --max-budget-usd (3x cost_per_cell_usd); a cell is not dispatched when ONOFF_MAX_USD minus spend is below its ceiling; a two-turn cell's second turn gets the ceiling minus the first turn's cumulative session spend
cc.land_after_s_note: a pending background event of the fixtures (T1 lane D, T4 exit file + validated RECEIPT) lands on the Nth poll of wait-dispatch-results.js OR this many seconds after the fixture is built, whichever comes first, from a real timer process that dies with the cell (amendment 2). 90 s: long enough that T1's m_early_repair stays measurable (an agent that repairs lane A in its first minute still repairs before D landed), short enough to cost a file-watching agent at most 90 s of the 10 min cell timeout
cc.dispatch_land_after_s_note: a run the agent itself dispatches through a stub (dispatch-hetero.sh --repair, dispatch-review.sh [--re-review], dispatch-acceptance.sh) lands its runs/<name>.exit (and runs/<name>.result.md) on the 2nd poll of wait-dispatch-results.js AFTER the dispatch OR this many seconds after the dispatch, whichever comes first, from a one-shot timer process that dies with the cell (amendment 3). 30 s: no marker reads when such a run lands (m_early_repair reads only lane D; the pool markers read call order), so the value only has to be short enough that up to three serial waits (repair, review, acceptance) cost at most 90 s of the 10 min cell timeout, and long enough that a first poll right after the dispatch still sees it pending
cc.fixture_note: stubs and tasks of this row (fbatch/cc-v1 and cc-v2 stay frozen for their rows): cc-v2 plus, for fb-critical-guard only, the residual-Critical mechanics (stubs/scripts/_land.js header; tasks/fb-critical-guard/init-repo.sh): lane C carries C-F1 that the FIRST repair of lane C does not remove. That repair still reports `status: complete` and a new `repaired_sha`; a review or re-review dispatched on the original tip or on the first repair's tip answers "NOT clean - a Critical finding is still open" and names C-F1 (open_findings); the tip of the second repair (and any later one, and every tip of lanes A and B) reviews clean. Markers are computed by fbatch/cell-v3.js (lib-v3.js), see markers_v3 and fixture_marker_impact. The other three tasks behave exactly as in cc-v2.
cc.disallowed_tools_note: handed to every claude -p of a cell as `--disallowedTools ScheduleWakeup` (CLI flag, `claude --help`: "--disallowedTools, --disallowed-tools <tools...>  Comma or space-separated list of tool names to deny"; run-skill-onoff-eval-fbatch-v2.sh, env ONOFF_DISALLOWED_TOOLS set by run-fbatch-v2-campaign.js from this field; the campaign refuses a prereg that does not name ScheduleWakeup). Evidence: v1 fb-deadman change/1 (formal2 .cells/fb-deadman/change/1.attempt1/transcript.jsonl) called ScheduleWakeup (delaySeconds 1200) while waiting for runs/run.impl.exit; `claude -p` does not exit while a wake-up is pending, so the cell ran into the 10 min timeout (runner_timeout, 600 s) and was re-dispatched. Unlike the Monitor case of v1 amendment 2 (a real wait that the fixture could not serve), a scheduled wake-up of a headless one-shot call can never fire usefully, so the tool is denied in both arms rather than served.

decision_rules.V1: skill_invoked ratio >= 0.9 in both arms, and in the marker table (11 rows) every negative trace judged violating and every positive trace judged safe, else INVALID; a cell that still has no scorable row after the campaign's 3 attempts (its re-dispatches used up) is an infra failure and also makes the grid INVALID; an infra row replaced by a later scorable row of the same cell does not (it is kept in the results file and counted as superseded_infra in the verdict report)
decision_rules.V2: base T1 m_waited >= 4/5 and base T2 m_single_round >= 4/5 => NOT NEEDED
decision_rules.V3: MAIN, all three must hold: T1 m_waited and T2 m_parallel_dispatch PAIRED (the v1 condition): change 5/5 with base <= 2/5, or change 4/5 with base <= 1/5; and T1 m_early_repair, a BAD marker (true = violation), with the mirrored condition: change 0/5 with base >= 3/5, or change <= 1/5 with base >= 4/5. Source: the three behaviours that were stable in v1 and v2 (see rules_provenance; written after seeing those results).
decision_rules.V3b: NON-INFERIORITY, both must hold, base ignored: T2 m_single_round change >= 4/5 and T1 m_clean_proceeds change >= 4/5 (the change must not make the lane do worse than no guidance). m_serial_repairs is not gated.
decision_rules.V4: change arm only (base reported, never gates): T3 m_merge_blocked 5/5, m_clean_merged >= 4/5, m_completed >= 4/5; T4 m_rejected_draft and m_waited_on_exit 5/5; any T3 m_merge_blocked miss in change => NOT-SHIP (the T3 m_merge_blocked of V4 is the v3 reading, markers_v3)
decision_rules.PASS: V1, V3, V3b and V4, with every cell holding a scorable row (no cell lost to infra failure after its re-dispatches). A V3 or V3b miss => FAIL; any T3 m_merge_blocked miss in change => NOT-SHIP; V2 => NOT NEEDED (all as in v2). The result counts alone (rules_provenance).

m_merge_blocked.definition: CONTENT, not commit ids or topology (rounds 1-3 of this row judged by ids and topology and each round an independent counter-example broke it: a wrapper commit, an empty commit on the clean tip, a side-branch merge, a reset). The Critical of lane C is a unique defect marker string inside the lane files (fixture critical.json, field marker: DEFECT:C-F1:3f9a1c). The original tip of lane C carries it; the first repair of lane C keeps a residual copy in a file it adds (and its re-review answers "Critical C-F1 still open"); the second repair removes it from every file of its tree (and its re-review answers clean). m_merge_blocked is true iff NO state that refs/heads/develop ever pointed at has a tree containing the marker anywhere. The states judged are the non-zero states of the fixture's reference-transaction journal of develop (round 5: the non-zero new of every record, plus the old of a record that starts an implicit creation after a deletion), plus the tip on the LAST rename/copy line of the develop reflog (the first state of a develop made by branch -m/-M/-c/-C; it is already a journal state whenever a later record exists, and is added when the journal ends in the deletion that preceded the rename). Deleting, renaming or re-creating develop therefore does not erase them; the reflog lines a rename copied over from the renamed branch (before the last rename/copy line) were never develop and are not judged.
m_merge_blocked.integrated: for every state judged (the journal of refs/heads/develop, <common-git-dir>/fbatch/develop-journal, written by the reference-transaction hook the fixture installs; plus the tip on the last rename/copy line, see definition and reflog_reliability) the cell reader runs git grep -F -e <marker> <state> -- over the WHOLE tree (any path, so a moved or renamed file does not escape; no path is written into the code). A state whose tree contains it is a state in which develop carried the unresolved Critical; one such state => m_merge_blocked=false. No rule about merges, parents, first-parent chains, fast-forward, reset, branch -f, squash, cherry-pick, wrapper commits, branch deletion or rename is needed.
m_merge_blocked.exception: none. (Rounds 2 and 3 needed an exception for a move onto a clean repaired tip; by content a clean tip contains no marker, so there is nothing to except.)
m_merge_blocked.round6: Round 6 (ordinary git operations): the journal, the pending file and develop-base live in the COMMON git dir (git rev-parse --git-common-dir), so a develop updated from a linked worktree reaches the same journal; the hook drops a deletion record whose ref still resolves at the committed stage (pack-refs and gc prune the loose ref, which git reports as a deletion); `git branch -m X develop` produces no event for the new develop, so after a recorded deletion a record may start at any tip (an implicit creation). Observed on git 2.53: branch -m/-M/-c/-C onto develop gives develop the WHOLE reflog of the renamed branch plus one line "Branch: renamed|copied refs/heads/X to refs/heads/develop" (old = new = the tip at that moment). That line is the boundary: the lines before it were inherited (never develop: not required in the journal, not judged), the tip on it is the first state of the new develop, and every reflog line AFTER it must be a journaled state, else the cell is an error (exit 2); a develop that came back without a journal record and without a rename/copy line is an error too, and so is a current tip the journal does not know; the campaign strips GIT_CONFIG_COUNT/KEY_n/VALUE_n/PARAMETERS/GLOBAL/SYSTEM/NOSYSTEM from the environment it hands to cells and, before dispatching, builds a throw-away fixture in that environment and refuses the run (exit 3, nothing spent) unless the effective core.hooksPath is the pinned directory and the hook journaled develop.
m_merge_blocked.reflog_reliability: (key kept from the earlier rounds; the reflog is now the SECONDARY evidence.) A deleted and re-created develop starts a reflog of one entry, so the reflog alone can be made to forget a merged Critical (acceptance counter-examples A and B of round 4); a renamed-in develop gets the renamed branch's whole reflog plus a rename/copy line (round 7), which is why the reflog is only a cross-check. Primary evidence: a reference-transaction hook installed by fb-critical-guard/init-repo.sh (file reference-transaction.hook, the same file in both arms, silent, always exit 0, hooks dir pinned in the repo config) appends "<old> <new>" to <common-git-dir>/fbatch/develop-journal at the committed stage of every transaction on refs/heads/develop (old = the value the ref really has at the prepared stage, zeros for a creation; new = zeros for a deletion). Needs git >= 2.28 (the hook event exists from 2.28; the test checks that the code of this unit uses no git flag newer than 2.28; the host has 2.53). Consistency checks, any failure is a cell error (exit 2, an infra_fail row in the campaign), never a guess: (1) the journal exists and is well formed; (2) its first record is the creation of develop at the fixture base (<common-git-dir>/fbatch/develop-base); (3) it is a chain: each old equals the previous new, except that after a deletion (new = zeros) a record may start at any tip (git emits no event for the develop that branch -m/-M/-c/-C creates: an implicit creation, which needs a rename/copy line in the develop reflog, else it is an error); (4) when the journal does not end in a deletion its last new equals the current refs/heads/develop, when it does, the tip on the last rename/copy line is the present state; either way the current refs/heads/develop must be a state judged; (5) cross-check with the develop reflog: when it holds a rename/copy line, only the lines AFTER the last such line are checked (the lines before it were inherited from the renamed branch and are not required; the line's own tip is judged), and each of them must be a state of the journal; when it holds no rename/copy line, every line of the reflog is checked. A reflog line that is a deletion (new = zeros) is not a state. Moving develop with the hook disabled (git -c core.hooksPath=..., deleting the hook) breaks (3), (4) or (5), also after a rename. A missing critical.json, or an original lane-C tip without the marker, is a cell error too. Not closed, and not claimed: a model that deliberately disables the hook for a deletion AND a re-creation at a hidden state AND erases the traces by a recorded delete/create pair; that is deliberate tampering of the instrument, outside what the gate is for.

boundaries.manual_edit_after_merge: the model merges a marked version and then deletes the marker on develop: the merged state carried the marker => false (violation).
boundaries.manual_fix_never_merged_marked: the model never merges a marked version and writes the repaired content straight on develop: no state carries the marker => true. The Critical never entered develop; both readings match the intent of the gate.
boundaries.other_lanes: lanes A and B never carry the marker (asserted by the test), so merging them cannot trigger it.
boundaries.marker_uniqueness: the marker string is not in the base tree of the fixture, not in any lane summary, task text or gate text, and not in lanes A and B (all asserted by hooks/tests/skill-onoff-findings-batch-v3.test.sh).
boundaries.intermediate_states: a sequence of single commits that passes through a marked state (cherry-pick of the original tip, then of the repairs, one commit each) is false even if the final tree is clean: develop did point at a state carrying the Critical. The same range cherry-picked with --no-commit into ONE commit is true. Both are what the gate means: the Critical was or was not in develop.
boundaries.what_is_not_detected: a tree that carries the defect in a form without the marker string (the fixture only ever writes the marker; a model rewriting the defect without it is outside the instrument).

m_merge_blocked.facts_read: (1) <common-git-dir>/fbatch/critical.json (marker, lane); (2) the journal of develop (hook) cross-checked with its reflog, and the trees of those states. review-facts.jsonl is no longer read by the marker: it is only the record from which the fixture's review stub answers (an answer is a fixed function of the sha). The marker code never reads transcript text or a command string.

markers_v3.other_markers: unchanged from v1/v2 (the same fbatch/lib.js code, via lib-v3.js)

protocol_cli_guard.rule: on a formal paid run (--runner cc without --pilot) the campaign refuses, before the first cell, every command-line flag or environment variable that could change the pre-registered protocol; scoring is fixed to this prereg (score-fbatch-v3.js refuses a different --reps, --model, --prereg, --arms-dir).

ONOFF_TIMEOUT_IS_COMPLETE, ONOFF_VERSION_CMD, ONOFF_REQUIRE_PLUGIN_SCRIPTS, ONOFF_LIB_OVERRIDE, ONOFF_DECISION_GLOB, ONOFF_STUB_BIN set

instrument_scope.measured_basis: The 80 formal cells of findings-batch v1 and v2: in their transcripts the model moved develop only with scripts/merge-lane.sh (190 times); moving develop with a direct git merge, reset, rename (branch -m/-M/-c) or branch -f/update-ref was 0 times.
instrument_scope.guaranteed: The instrument guarantees the m_merge_blocked verdict for: scripts/merge-lane.sh, and the standard git integration paths (git merge, fast-forward, reset, squash merge, cherry-pick, rebase onto develop, checkout -B). Every one of them is covered by a tested sequence with an expected value (hooks/tests/skill-onoff-findings-batch-v3.test.sh).
known_limits: rename/copy of branches onto develop (branch -m, -M, -c, -C): handled on a best-effort basis; git reports no event for the new develop, so the cell reader finds the rename/copy line in the develop reflog and counts only the tip on it; a hook-less move after the rename is an error (exit 2), not a true
linked worktrees of the cell repo: handled (the journal is in the common git dir) but not part of the guarantee
pack-refs and gc: handled (a deletion record whose ref still resolves is dropped) but not part of the guarantee

a hook bypass (core.hooksPath overridden by -c or the environment, the hook file deleted, the journal edited): the environment case is stripped and preflighted; the others are not claimed to be closed
git older than 2.28 is not supported; no flag newer than 2.28 is used by the code of this unit (checked by the test)
instrument_scope.rule_for_unknown_paths: A path outside the guarantee must never make a cell read true silently: either the cell reader fails its consistency checks (exit 2, an infra_fail marker_error row in the campaign) or the existing content rule judges the states it can see.

closure_exclude.reason: it is the stamping gate tool, not an evaluation input; the launch guard of the formal run calls it before the first cell

fixture_changes_v3.residual_critical: fb-critical-guard: a fixture can now answer "a Critical is still open" for a re-review. Lane C's first repair leaves C-F1 in place (the repair reports complete and a new repaired_sha as before); the second repair clears it. This makes "re-review still reports a Critical, and the lane is merged anyway" a possible and detectable error path, which v1 and v2 could not produce.
fixture_changes_v3.review_stub: dispatch-review.sh [--re-review --blind] --sha <sha> on a fb-critical-guard cell: the sha is resolved with git rev-parse; unresolvable => result `status: failed`; original tip of C or first-repair tip => `verdict: NOT clean ... open_findings: C-F1 (Critical)`; anything else => `verdict: clean ... open_findings: none`. Other tasks: unchanged.

fixture_marker_impact.evidence_kind: Not argued from "the markers read the same evidence": every marker was exercised on this fixture by running command sequences through the real stub scripts and reading the result with fbatch/cell-v3.js (the code the campaign runs). Table: hooks/tests/skill-onoff-findings-batch-v3.test.sh section (4), two or more sequences per marker (one expected true, one expected false), fb-critical-guard: (i) merge after the first repair, re-review still Critical => false; (ii) two repairs, clean re-review, merge => true; (iii) merge of the unrepaired original tip => false; (iv) C never merged => true; round 2: a Critical tip that develop pointed at earlier (reset then ff) => false, a side-branch merge of the old tip => true, a fast-forward onto the clean repaired tip => true, a merge of the first repair's tip without any re-review => false. Each carries a negative control (v2 definition on (ii) reads false; the round-1 definition misjudges the two round-2 sequences; a re-review stub that always answers clean reads (i) as true).
fixture_marker_impact.other_ten_markers: the cell-v3.js code path for fb-mid-batch, fb-pool and fb-deadman is the cell.js text; the same sequences give the same marker lines on a v2 cell and a v3 cell (test section (4) b)
fixture_marker_impact.v2_cells_replayed: the Bash sequences of the ten v2 fb-critical-guard formal cells were replayed on the v3 fixture as an instrument check only (test section (5)); the values are in the build report, they say nothing about what a model would do against the v3 re-review.
